Interferon gamma assays were more sensitive than tuberculin skin testing for diagnosis of Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection in HIV infected patients.

the development of an innovative and highly sensitive method for the diagnosis of latent TB infection (LTBI).

the use of IGRAs in addition to TST increases the number of diagnoses of LTBI in HIV-infected individuals, and that the use of both IGRA tests increases this figure further.
the use of IGRAs in addition to TST may be useful in some HIV-infected patients, but not in the whole group of HIV-infected individuals.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of IGRAs is useful for the diagnosis of M. Tuberculosis in HIV-infected individuals, and the combination of IGRAs and tuberculin test is the optimal strategy for the diagnosis of latent TB in these individuals.

1) TST is not a useful tool for the diagnosis of M. tuberculosisis infection in HIV-inferscted individuals; 2) QFG and TSPOT.TB are useful for the diagnosis of latent TB infection in HIV-infested individuals; and 3) the best strategy for the diagnosis of Latent TB infection in HIV patients would be to perform TST and QFG or TSPOT.Tb in parallel.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of IGRAs in HIV-infected individuals may be a useful approach to improve the identification of LTBI.
IGRAs are useful in the diagnosis of LTBi in HIV-infected persons.
IGRAs may have a higher specificity and sensitivity than TST for LTBI in HIV-infected subjects, and that dual sequential testing with TSPOT.TB or QFG may be the optimal strategy for LTBI screening.
